paragraphs.text: A [Zhengshan Xiaozhong](lapsang:definition) made in 1934 in Tongmu village, in the Wuyi Mountains of Fujian. Tongmu is the place usually given as the [birthplace of red tea](lapsang:history), the fully oxidised tea that English calls [black](red:definition). This lot was made by the Tongmu method of the Republican years. It was smoked over pine, rolled by hand and dried over a wood fire. In that way of working the leaf lies on bamboo mats in a [qinglou](lapsang:smoke), a wooden drying house with the fire at the bottom, so the heat and smoke rise through it.

At ninety-two years it stands outside any described practice. Lapsang has [no recognised tradition of long ageing](lapsang:ageing), and the trade names no category of decades-old red tea. What it does record is the first few years in good storage, when the pine smoke softens. This leaf has gone far beyond that, and it is a record of how the village made tea long before the trade of today.

brewing.text: In a cup or pot, use about 3 grams for 240 ml, with water at 90 to 100°C, and steep about two to five minutes, usually around three. Gongfu style, use about 5 grams in a 100 to 110 ml gaiwan or pot, with short steeps that grow a little longer each round. Too hot or too long and the smoke turns harsh and bitter and covers the tea.

notice.text: The smoke softer and further back, with dried fruit coming forward.
